what_was_found: A refused card payment returned the client to the sign-in page; the refusal was PAYMENT_ACCOUNT_CURRENCY (a GBP test account, a USD package), right at confirm and wrong at listing.
The Free package had no limit and was granted again after its allowance ran out (07:15, 07:24, 07:43 the same Client); a new package's default made a priced package once-per-client too.
Sessions recorded PRINCIPAL for every email, phone or social sign-in; the channel or provider was kept nowhere.

Walled garden, measured from a device that had not signed in: every port open to every garden address (80, QUIC, any TCP port), a rule's Ports stored and ignored, the baseline resolvers reachable on 443 (DNS over HTTPS), and a mail service's address also serving YouTube, Search, Drive, Docs and Translate.
A one-time code was single-use but not device-bound: any device holding the code, or the email's link that carries it over plain HTTP on the client LAN, could verify it.
IPv6 forwarding enabled on the host with no ip6 rule in the StayConnect table; no client receives a v6 address and nothing is reachable over v6 today (latent).
delivered: A refused acquisition re-renders package selection signed in, with the reason; the landing page continues an unfinished journey at /packages for the commerce session's lifetime.

Card is offered only in a currency an ACTIVE payment account settles (SiteMethods.CardCurrencies); the Admin Console says which packages are withheld and why, on Payment methods and in the package editor.

A new Free package defaults to once per client, a new priced package to repeatable; the default follows the price until the operator chooses; existing packages keep their rules. The PRE-LIVE Free package was republished (revision 13) once per client through the audited publish route.

Migration 0109: a credential label on auth_contexts and principal_device_credentials (EMAIL_OTP, SMS_OTP, WHATSAPP_OTP, SOCIAL_<provider>, VOUCHER, ACCOUNT, OPEN) copied onto sessions.credential_method; sessions carry package_acquisitions; the sessions screen and the dashboard read the words.
Reading the code: email-service presets and bounded custom host names under Sign-in methods, opened only while Email code is on, resolved through the guest resolver (unbound).

Walled garden in three sets: address-only rules keep every port; (address, port) pairs for a rule's Ports, TCP 443/993/5228/5223 for an email service, TCP 443 for identity providers and payment pages, port 53 only for the baseline resolvers; planned by one pure function, synced in one transaction, carried across a netd structural replace.
Migration 0110: a one-time code is bound at issue to the kernel-resolved MAC of the device that asked; another device is refused before the code is compared, no attempt counted, in six languages.

security_findings_open: Address-based filtering cannot isolate a domain behind a shared front end: with an email service open, the other services its addresses serve answer on 443 to a device that has not signed in. Two bounded designs are written in the contract (10.1) for decision: a per-device, time-boxed verification window restricted to the mail services (recommended), or TLS server-name filtering. IPv6 forwarding with no ip6 policy is recorded for decision. DNS tunnelling through the guest resolver is an inherent captive-portal property, recorded, not changed.
financial: No financial change. The presentment-vs-settlement currency design (provider-managed conversion with the provider's rate, fee, net and balance-transaction id recorded on the settlement) is a recommendation in the contract (9) and needs the Product Owner's decision; PAYMENT_ACCOUNT_CURRENCY keeps refusing a mismatch and the method is withheld at listing. payment_transactions on PRE-LIVE remains unchanged.
